correctness.rationale: Radical nilpotence lifts exactly; uniform quotient reduces arbitrary finite ring to simple matrix factors. Conditioning on a rank-r partial product, uniform restriction to its image has nilpotency probability q^(-r), independently proved by Fitting decomposition. This equals its kernel probability on a uniform vector, reducing k random matrices to k successive nonzero-survival trials. The decay/exponential peeling argument rigorously reconstructs the full multiset from all P_k. Exact arithmetic exhaustive tests for four independent finite examples pass. Domain includes k=1 and n=1; no finite extrapolation is used.

value.rationale: The motivating 2026 nilpotent product invariant had exact classification only for two-factor commutative settings; here a complete invariant for arbitrary finite associative unital rings over all product lengths is given, including a converse criterion that classifies precisely when two different rings are indistinguishable by every nilpotence probability. The simple-module size classification and radical invariance have direct structural meaning, not an arbitrary numeric slice or routine restatement of one known instance.
